entries.clue: Incarceration's a bit like a dessert topping, it's said (7)

indicatorNotes.it's said: what is said is heard rather than read, so go by the pronunciation

blocks.clueFragment: a bit like a dessert topping
blocks.note: custard-y: rather like custard, the classic pudding topping

annotation.surface: Someone compares a prison stretch to a pudding.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is a made-up adjective: something custardy is custard-like, and in a non-rhotic British accent it is pronounced just like custody.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: custody is the state of being held by the police or in prison.

entries.clue: Lee's debut secured by having fresh set of  Dracula teeth? Too modern (10)

indicatorNotes.debut: a debut is a first appearance, so take the first letter
indicatorNotes.secured by: something secured by another is held fast inside it

blocks.clueFragment: having fresh set of  Dracula teeth
blocks.note: new-fanged: with new fangs, the teeth of a vampire like Dracula

annotation.surface: Christopher Lee, the actor famous as Dracula, gets a fresh set of fangs for his first film.
annotation.walkthrough: Christopher Lee played Dracula in the Hammer horror films, which is what makes the surface hang together. NEWFANGED is not a real word; it is invented so the L can turn it into one.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: newfangled is the grumpy word for anything too new to be trusted.

entries.clue: War's end included in settler's entreaty (6)

indicatorNotes.end: the end of a word is its last letter
indicatorNotes.included in: something included in another goes inside it

annotation.surface: A pioneer pleads for the fighting to stop.
annotation.walkthrough: A settler suggests a colonist, but here it is someone who settles an account.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an entreaty is an earnest plea, and a prayer is a plea made to a god.

entries.clue: see 26dn.
Note: Rex has 'doo-dah' that's no longer tender (8)

blocks.note: the fourth note of the sol-fa scale
both are words for something you cannot name

annotation.surface: A king has an unnamed something that has become tough, or perhaps no longer sore.
annotation.walkthrough: Tender here means legal tender, money a shop must accept. A farthing was a quarter of an old British penny, withdrawn in 1961.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the old farthing coin was withdrawn in 1961 and stopped being legal tender.

entries.clue: Trainer's small tool? (4)

annotation.surface: A coach owns a little implement.
annotation.walkthrough: Trainer suggests a coach, but a trainer is also a sports shoe, the British word for a sneaker.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a trainer, the British name for a sneaker, is one kind of footwear.

entries.clue: Sunak's beginning to be crushed by Right – boom! (7)

indicatorNotes.beginning: the beginning of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.crushed by: something crushed by another is squeezed in its middle

annotation.surface: Rishi Sunak is flattened by the right wing of his party with a bang.
annotation.walkthrough: Right looks like the political right, but it means correct, PROPER. Boom is a verb here, as in an economy booming.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: a booming business is one that thrives.

entries.clue: Turn up a hunter's pants (7)

indicatorNotes.pants: British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a mess to be sorted

annotation.surface: A hunter's trousers are discovered.
annotation.walkthrough: Pants looks like underwear, but in British slang it also means rubbish, which signals rearranging.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to turn up a lost item is to dig it out, which is literally what unearthing does.

entries.clue: Ambitious types of alien UFOs? Help! (8)

indicatorNotes.alien: the letters become strange and foreign, so rearrange them

annotation.surface: Someone cries for help at the sight of flying saucers.
annotation.walkthrough: Alien fits the UFO picture so well that it hides its job as the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: such people are aspiring to succeed, like would-be candidates in a contest.

entries.clue: Kinky material puts energy into soap? (7)

indicatorNotes.into: and that place is inside the other part

annotation.surface: Someone adds oomph to a steamy soap opera.
annotation.walkthrough: Soap suggests a TV soap opera, but it is the foam, LATHER.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this hide is the classic material of fetish clothing, hence kinky.

entries.clue: Difficult part of golf course, said to be like pubic hair? (5)

indicatorNotes.said: what is said is heard rather than read, so go by the pronunciation

blocks.note: a tough tee: a hard spot to drive off from

annotation.surface: A golfer grumbles that the rough is as scratchy as a certain kind of hair.
annotation.walkthrough: The difficult part of a golf course looks like the rough, but it is a tough tee, the place each hole starts from.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: such hair grows in tufts.

entries.clue: Futile instruction to cut the digital gesturing (9)

blocks.note: pointing with a digit, a finger
less! is an order to reduce

annotation.surface: A futile request to stop someone jabbing their finger.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an order: point less, meaning do less pointing. Digital means with the fingers, not electronic.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a futile effort has no purpose at all.

entries.clue: Top level fallout when diamonds added to collar (8)

annotation.surface: Nuclear fallout spreads at the top of government when jewels are pinned to a collar.
annotation.walkthrough: Top level fallout sounds like political or nuclear fallout, but it is flakes falling from the top of your head, often onto a collar.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the flakes of skin fall out from the top level of the body, the scalp.

entries.clue: Morgan's endless, empty, cackle – prick! (6)

indicatorNotes.endless: a word without its end has lost its final letter
indicatorNotes.empty: an empty word has had its contents removed, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: Piers Morgan, the TV presenter: first name without its last letter

annotation.surface: An insult hurled at Piers Morgan for his endless, hollow cackling.
annotation.walkthrough: Morgan stands for his first name, Piers. Prick looks like an insult closing the rant, but it is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to prick a balloon is to puncture it.

entries.clue: (& 24dn.) Group of supporters poisoned by Trump, turn appreciably sick (10)

annotation.definition: Group of supporters poisoned by Trump

indicatorNotes.sick: the letters are unwell, disordered, and must be rearranged

annotation.surface: Donald Trump's followers, having taken his poison, grow visibly ill.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across two grid entries: REPUBLICAN here and PARTY at 24 down. All fifteen letters of turn appreciably are used.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the US party whose supporters, the setter says, Trump has poisoned.

entries.clue: Weight-watcher / a mouth opening = part of girth calculation (8)

indicatorNotes.opening: the opening of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A slimmer's equation for working out a waistline.
annotation.walkthrough: The slash marks where A and M go into DIETER; the clue gives no word for inserting, so the layout does the job.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: girth, a circumference, is calculated as pi times this width.

entries.clue: Boris's duff economic policy, in bizarre leg-pull vein (9-2)

indicatorNotes.bizarre: the letters come out strange and need rearranging

annotation.surface: Boris Johnson's flagship policy is mocked as an odd practical joke.
annotation.walkthrough: A leg-pull is a practical joke, which is what the surface calls the policy.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: this was Boris Johnson's slogan for spreading prosperity to poorer British regions.

entries.clue: Hugo sits on one at première of African Queen (8)

indicatorNotes.sits on: in a down answer, a part that sits on another comes above it

annotation.surface: A novelist attends the opening night of the film The African Queen.
annotation.walkthrough: The African Queen is a 1951 film, which glues the surface together; Queen alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the monarch who reigned over Britain from 1837 to 1901.

entries.clue: A former Secretary of State pocketing duke's loan (7)

indicatorNotes.pocketing: one part slips another into its pocket

blocks.note: A plus Cyrus Vance, US Secretary of State under Carter

annotation.surface: A retired statesman trousers a nobleman's loan.
annotation.walkthrough: Duke's reads as possessive, but the 's joins the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: money handed over before it is due, much like a loan.

entries.clue: Caught in lie about government's top upper limit (7)

indicatorNotes.about: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards
indicatorNotes.top: in a down answer the top of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A government is caught out lying about its spending cap.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces are not in clue order: IN comes after the turned-round LIE in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: the top of a room, extended to any cap such as a price or debt limit.

entries.clue: Balls trapped in Channel dock? (6)

indicatorNotes.trapped in: something trapped in another is caught inside it

blocks.note: a channel for fluid or air
Ed Balls, the former Labour minister

annotation.surface: Footballs get stuck in a harbour on the English Channel.
annotation.walkthrough: Balls is a surname: Ed Balls is a British Labour politician turned TV personality. Dock is a verb, as in docking pay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: docking someone's pay means taking money off it.

entries.clue: Cordial's a help to singers? Clever (8)

annotation.surface: A fruit drink is praised as good for the voice.
annotation.walkthrough: Cordial looks like a soothing drink for the throat, but it is the adjective meaning friendly.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: cordial relations are warm and friendly ones.

entries.clue: Copper gets dude to isolate (3,3)

blocks.note: a toff is a posh, dandyish man

annotation.surface: A police officer gets a man to be kept apart.
annotation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer, but it is the metal. A toff is British slang for an upper-class man.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: a village severed from the world by floods is isolated.

entries.clue: see 15dn.
Playing truant, so a candidate for a rocket at rear? (9)

annotation.definition: candidate for a rocket at rear

indicatorNotes.Playing: the letters play around into a new order

annotation.surface: A pupil skipping school deserves a rocket up the backside.
annotation.walkthrough: A rocket is British slang for a severe telling-off. The definition turns this round: a space traveller rides a rocket firing at the rear.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a space traveller is a natural passenger for a rocket propelled from its rear.

entries.clue: (& 4dn.) Ex-PM's only a bit useless, right? (4)

indicatorNotes.useless: letters in a useless state are wrecked and need putting back in order

annotation.surface: A sly aside that a former prime minister was only somewhat useless.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is split across two grid entries: TONY here and BLAIR at 4 down. The clue reads as a political jab, while useless is really the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Tony Blair led Labour and was British Prime Minister from 1997 to 2007.

entries.clue: Fabric of time diminished royal (5)

indicatorNotes.diminished: a diminished name is cut down to a shorter form

annotation.surface: A member of the royal family is worn down by the passing years.
annotation.walkthrough: Diminished here means reduced to a nickname: Will for William.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a woven cloth with diagonal ribs, used for denim and chinos.

entries.clue: Can resident politician Vic start to testify? (7)

indicatorNotes.start: the start of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A local asks whether a politician called Vic may begin giving evidence.
annotation.walkthrough: Can is not the verb but slang for prison, so a can resident is a prisoner.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense: the can is prison, and its resident is someone serving a sentence there.

entries.clue: Forbear's infra-red balls died off (7)

indicatorNotes.balls: slang for nonsense, so the letters are jumbled
indicatorNotes.off: died gives D, and off says take it away

annotation.surface: An ancestor's heat-seeking balls have dropped off.
annotation.walkthrough: Forbear looks like forebear, an ancestor, but it is the verb meaning hold back.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to forbear from something is to hold back from doing it.
